name: WASH-related disease burden estimation tool (country tool)
owner: World Health Organization (WASH and Health Unit)
what_it_converts: WASH exposure distributions into attributable deaths and DALYs for diarrhoea ARI undernutrition and STH with scenario comparison
inputs: Population and disease burden (WHO GHE) by country; share of population at each water sanitation and hygiene exposure level (JMP categories plus point-of-use treatment type); user scenarios
outputs: Population attributable fractions; attributable deaths and DALYs; mortality rate (SDG 3.9.2); difference between two scenarios
platform: Excel workbook (sheets: Cover note Scenario SDG Scenario ALT Difference Exposures Population and GHE Nutrition PAF)
licence: WHO copyright; no open licence stated on the page
strengths: Same method and relative risks as the WHO 2023 global estimates (Wolf 2022 Wolf 2018 Ross 2023); scenario logic is the natural core of an ex-ante calculator; country data pre-loaded
limits: Works at population level not at enterprise or household-year level; exposure categories are JMP service levels and treatment types not enterprise outputs; no uncertainty propagation beyond CIs; spreadsheet formulas not versioned code
relevance_to_afa_tool: High: the conversion logic to reuse (PAF based) and a reference to validate against

name: Jal Jeevan Mission health impact simulation
owner: World Health Organization for the Government of India
what_it_converts: Projected coverage of safely managed drinking water into diarrhoea deaths and DALYs averted and a monetary value
inputs: Baseline exposure (NSS 2018 and programme data); programme and business-as-usual coverage trajectories; WHO GHE diarrhoea burden; UN population; relative risks from Wolf 2022
outputs: Annual diarrhoea deaths and DALYs under two scenarios; deaths and DALYs averted (almost 400000 lives and 14 million DALYs); economic value (3 x GDP per capita per DALY; up to USD 101 billion); time savings
platform: Slide deck and the WHO country tool
strengths: Worked example of an ex-ante programme level application of the WHO method incl. valuation
limits: Programme scale only; linear coverage projection; valuation by GDP multiple is contested
relevance_to_afa_tool: High as a worked example of the method

name: Lives Saved Tool (LiST)
owner: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health with Avenir Health (Spectrum)
what_it_converts: Coverage change of child health interventions including WASH into child deaths averted and lives saved
inputs: National coverage of interventions (incl. improved water source water connection in home improved sanitation handwashing with soap hygienic disposal of stools) cause of death structure and population
outputs: Deaths averted by cause and intervention; mortality rates; stunting effects
licence: Free to use; licence terms not stated on the site
strengths: Established mortality model used by governments and donors; WASH effect sizes documented in Darvesh 2017 and Fischer Walker 2022; country data pre-loaded
limits: Mortality only (no cases); national or subnational coverage changes not enterprise outputs; effect sizes fixed inside the model
relevance_to_afa_tool: Medium: a benchmark for mortality conversion and a reference for the effect values

name: GiveWell water quality cost-effectiveness analysis
what_it_converts: Chlorination programme reach (dispensers and in-line chlorination) into under-five deaths averted morbidity reduction and cost per outcome
inputs: Programme coverage and cost; pooled trial mortality effect (14 percent then adjusted to 6 to 11 percent); adult mortality scaling; diarrhoea morbidity; development effects
outputs: Deaths averted; cost per death averted; units of value compared with cash transfers
platform: Public web page with linked spreadsheets
strengths: Transparent adjustments (bundling internal validity scaling to over-fives); explicit uncertainty discussion; ties to Kremer et al. 2023
limits: Mortality focused; chlorination only; funder-specific value judgements
relevance_to_afa_tool: Medium: template for adjustment factors and for communicating uncertainty

name: Water treatment and child mortality meta-analysis and cost-effectiveness analysis
owner: Kremer Luby Maertens Tan Wiecek (NBER working paper 30835)
what_it_converts: Water treatment coverage into expected deaths and DALYs averted per person and cost per DALY
inputs: Pooled mortality odds ratio (OR 0.72; posterior predictive RR 0.75); programme costs for chlorine dispensers and coupons; baseline mortality
outputs: Expected deaths averted per person 0.015 (dispensers) and 0.007 (coupons); DALYs per person; cost per DALY about USD 40
platform: Working paper with Bayesian model code (R)
licence: Working paper; code availability to confirm
strengths: Only pooled mortality estimate for water treatment; explicit heterogeneity handling (prediction for a new setting)
limits: Not peer reviewed at the time of reading; chlorination studies dominate; morbidity not modelled

name: Economics of Sanitation Initiative (ESI)
owner: World Bank Water and Sanitation Program
what_it_converts: Sanitation deficits into economic losses (health time access tourism) by country
inputs: National sanitation coverage; disease incidence and deaths; cost of illness; time losses
outputs: Annual economic cost of poor sanitation (USD and percent of GDP) by country; benefit-cost ratios of options
licence: Reports open on World Bank and SuSanA; tool files not public
strengths: Country level cost of poor sanitation incl. health; benefit-cost ratios per option (Vietnam rural pit latrine 6 to 1)
limits: Dated (2005 to 2010 data); national not enterprise; method documents dispersed
relevance_to_afa_tool: Medium: valuation side of an ex-ante case

name: WHO global cost-benefit analyses of water and sanitation (Hutton and Haller 2004; Hutton 2012; Hutton and Chase 2016)
owner: World Health Organization and World Bank
what_it_converts: Coverage improvements into health benefits time savings and benefit-cost ratios by region
inputs: Coverage targets; intervention costs; relative risks from reviews; time savings; cost of illness
outputs: Benefit-cost ratios (global about 4 to 1 for sanitation about 2 for water in 2012); costs per DALY
strengths: Standard reference numbers for benefit-cost ratios; transparent assumptions
limits: Regional averages; dated inputs; not transaction level

name: WASHCost calculator
what_it_converts: Life-cycle costs and service levels of water and sanitation services
inputs: Capital and recurrent expenditure by component; service level indicators (9 water 10 sanitation)
outputs: Cost per person per year by service level; comparisons across technologies and countries
strengths: Service level ladder thinking; cost benchmarks from India Burkina Faso Ghana Mozambique
limits: No health outcomes; tool appears unmaintained
relevance_to_afa_tool: Low for health; relevant for cost inputs and the service level framing

name: 3ie WASH evidence gap map (2014 2018 2020 updates and 2023 REAPER map)
owner: International Initiative for Impact Evaluation (3ie) with WSSCC and Campbell
what_it_converts: Maps impact evaluations and systematic reviews by intervention and outcome
outputs: Interactive map (359 impact evaluations and 43 systematic reviews in 2020 update) with confidence ratings
strengths: Fast way to see where evidence exists by intervention and outcome; links to reviews
limits: Not a calculator; coverage ends 2020 for health outcomes
relevance_to_afa_tool: Medium: source of studies and of the evidence strength map

name: IRIS+ WASH impact theme and core metrics (Navigating Impact)
owner: Global Impact Investing Network (GIIN) with Water.org and WaterEquity
what_it_converts: Standardised output and outcome metrics for WASH investments (no health conversion)
outputs: Metrics such as WASH facilities type (PD3668) availability of basic services (PI0617) public water point coverage (PI3218) aligned to JMP ladder
platform: Web catalogue (metric details behind sign-in for core sets)
strengths: Investor vocabulary; JMP service level alignment; can carry the tool's input metrics
limits: No health outcome estimation; core metric sets need registration
relevance_to_afa_tool: Medium: align tool inputs to IRIS+ codes

name: e-MFP WASH Action Group indicator framework
owner: European Microfinance Platform with Aqua for All (Jeroen Trimpe Burger)
what_it_converts: Indicator set for impact investors at SME and financial institution level
outputs: 12 indicators and 44 sub-indicators incl. 2.2 Reduction in infection diseases / improved health (SME level) and 2.2 Number of investments leading to improved health (FI level); water and sanitation specific indicators
platform: PDF framework; data collection tool to be developed
strengths: Already adopted by Aqua for All's investor network; names health as an indicator; field tested with four FIs
limits: Health indicator is undefined (no method or evidence base); self-reported data; no conversion
relevance_to_afa_tool: High: the tool should define how indicator 2.2 is computed

name: Impact-Linked Finance design principles and learnings (Roots of Impact)
what_it_converts: Guidance on structuring ILF transactions (incentives to the value creator outcomes over outputs impact additionality)
outputs: Design principles; a planned open-source ILF self-assessment questionnaire; baseline projection guidance
strengths: Defines additionality as rewards for results that would not occur without them; stresses baseline projections and outcome proxies when outcomes are not measurable
limits: No quantitative additionality method; no health evidence

name: SIINC for WASH transaction documents (KWSH 2021; ACK snapshot 2024; SIINC leaflet 2025)
owner: Aqua for All with Roots of Impact
what_it_converts: Verified enterprise outputs into outcome payments (no health conversion)
inputs: Enterprise metrics (e.g. share of connected households in licence areas low-income customers reached)
strengths: Shows the metrics the tool must accept as inputs and the verification practice already in place
limits: Metrics are outputs; no health pathway
relevance_to_afa_tool: High: defines the input side of the tool

name: Cambodia Rural Sanitation Development Impact Bond
owner: iDE with USAID (outcome payer) and Stone Family Foundation (investor)
what_it_converts: Open defecation free village status into outcome payments
inputs: Village ODF claims cross-checked with government data
outputs: Outcome payments up to USD 10 million; 1780 villages and about 500000 households
strengths: Precedent for outcome payments on verified sanitation outcomes in an Aqua for All country
limits: Output and coverage based; no health outcome metric; self-reported monitoring with cross-checks

name: UK WASH Results Programme payment by results (evaluation and verification guidance)
what_it_converts: Verified outputs (people reached) into payments; independent verification of supplier data
inputs: Supplier monitoring data verified by a third party
outputs: People reached with water sanitation and hygiene; lessons on PbR design
strengths: Largest PbR precedent in WASH; verification system documented; Howard and White 2020 academic review
limits: Outputs not health outcomes; incentives favoured tried approaches

name: Averted DALYs as a performance indicator for water quality interventions (review)
owner: Water (MDPI) review by Gwenzi and colleagues (W2807271110)
what_it_converts: Reviews CRA and QMRA routes to compute averted DALYs for water quality interventions
inputs: Exposure and dose-response data (QMRA) or relative risks and coverage (CRA)
outputs: Averted DALYs per intervention; discussion of challenges
strengths: Methods comparison relevant to the tool's design choice (CRA with pooled RRs versus QMRA)

name: Fischer Walker 2022 updated assumptions for LiST (WASH and diarrhoea morbidity)
what_it_converts: Updated effect sizes of household WASH interventions on diarrhoea morbidity for LiST
strengths: Documents the WASH values LiST carries

name: mWater platform
what_it_converts: Monitoring platform for water and sanitation assets and surveys (named in the ToR as a preferred platform)
platform: Web and mobile app; free tier
licence: Platform terms; free for governments and NGOs
strengths: Widely used in Aqua for All countries; could host the input side and dashboards
limits: No health conversion logic; calculation would sit outside or as custom indicators
